output.name: Tirun

rear planks of the hull's curve

output.myth: Tirun came home keel-up in the spring gale, with no crew aboard and her lamp still lit underneath. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, went down the tally and found eleven names missing and no reel that had let them go. Tavo the Gale laughed when the old women asked him, and said he had only lifted the boat, not drowned anyone. Aun, who cut the string, would not say what he had seen. Ennu the Kite-Wright came with bone and cloth and turned the hull over to look. Under the planks there was a lamp, trimmed by someone careful, and nobody in the islands can say whose hands. So the boat sits up in Vel with its light under the keel. When the wind is wrong, the old ones say, you can see that light moving beneath it, like someone still bailing, still counting, still looking for the way home.
output.verse:
Keel-up in the dark,
a lamp still burns beneath her
no hands to bail her.

problems: The blind guess reads it as a dome/leaf or bowl-like outline with a ring-marked star, and the tether-to-lantern idea is close. But the figure is ambiguous as a hull and the balloon-with-tether alternative is the closer read, so match is only 3.
Stern tip (116247) and rear planks (115669) sit almost on top of each other near (160, 220). The two parts are not separated, so the figure does not read as two distinct points on the hull.
Midships (114375) lies on the upper arc near (218, 240), not on the underside of the hull, so the part assignment is wrong.
Labels overlap badly: the crown, stern, rear-planks and bow-rim labels collide near (130-360, 205-230), which makes the drawing hard to read.
The hull outline is two thin blue curves with a faint, uncertain upturn. It is not clearly an upturned hull, and the 'upturned' arch is not obvious. Orientation is unclear.
The lantern star 113368 at about (263, 383) is ringed and linked by the gold tether from bow foot 114119 at about (230, 283). That part works and is the strongest element.
The gold line is only the tether, so the hull is drawn with blue lines rather than being a copy of the gold lines. That is acceptable.
judge.advice: Redraw the hull as a clearly upturned boat: a convex arch on top with the crown of the keel (115438) at the highest point, roughly near (190, 210). Run the underside as a flatter curve below it. Spread the stern tip (116247) to the far left tip near (120, 238) and move the rear planks (115669) onto the lower-left curve near (140, 255), so they are not stacked. Put midships (114375) on the lower underside curve near (200, 262). Put the bow-side rim (114341) where the curve turns down on the right, near (215, 240). Keep bow foot (114119) at about (230, 283) as the tether anchor. Keep the lantern (113368) at about (263, 383) with its ring and the gold tether. Shorten or offset the labels so they do not overlap: place crown and stern labels above the hull and midships and bow labels below it. Keep the lantern tether straight and downward from the bow foot.
